# Ternuxx

**Repository:** [`soobujmiah/ternuxx`](https://github.com/soobujmiah/ternuxx). Use `./ternuxx` from a source checkout or `bin/ternuxx` directly.

**বাংলা:** Pocket-এ mobile workstation তৈরির স্বাধীন project। Native Termux layer compatible tools ও Android-facing integration-এর সুযোগ দেবে; বিদ্যমান Ternux Debian PRoot layer Linux desktop, established workload ও configured GPU path দেবে। Hybrid mode দুটিকে নিরাপদ handoff দিয়ে এক workstation-এ যুক্ত করবে।

**English:** I want my phone to be a workstation I can carry in my pocket. I want native Termux and my existing Ternux PRoot setup to work together, so I can use each where it fits. Read [what I have in mind](docs/PRODUCT-VISION.md).

## Planned use

- **Native mode:** compatible Termux packages and Android-facing workflows, subject to package, API, permission, and device support.
- **Existing Ternux PRoot:** opt-in execution of selected Linux workloads in the existing Debian guest. Ternuxx will not own or clean up that desktop session.
- **Hybrid mode:** future explicit routing between those providers and verified accelerator backends, while preserving the existing Ternux PRoot feature set.

The existing [Ternux project](https://github.com/soobujmiah/ternux) remains independent. Its PRoot features remain a first-class part of the combined workstation; Ternuxx does not modify, minimize, or replace its launcher or rootfs. Native and PRoot strengths complement each other. NPU support is a research/verification gate, not yet a claim.

## Development notes

`install` uses a preview-first Termux APT transaction and persists full dependency plans under private Ternuxx state; its approved 2026-10-18 XFCE install is recorded with all 77 package versions in the P2 evidence. P2 is complete for the recorded target; the original pre-consent console capture remains a historical gap, while a later target-native preview revalidation verifies the current approval binding without applying another package transaction. P3 is active, and the Ternux PRoot lifecycle/workload adapter remains unimplemented; a read-only companion diagnostic can verify selected guest display/audio/renderer context. The tested native Termux Turnip package rejected Adreno 825; this does not invalidate the separately configured Ternux PRoot graphics route. See [research and evidence](docs/RESEARCH.md), [installation status](docs/INSTALLATION.md), [PRoot GPU reuse](docs/PROOT-GPU.md), and the [existing workstation preservation baseline](docs/evidence/2026-10-18-existing-workstation-baseline.md).

See [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), [Native/PRoot integration](docs/HYBRID-INTEGRATION.md), [Native Wine and Hangover](docs/WINE-NATIVE.md), [workload optimization](docs/OPTIMIZATION.md), [documentation and SKB sync](docs/KNOWLEDGE-SYNC.md), [Installation status](docs/INSTALLATION.md), and [AI assistant instructions](AI_ASSISTANT.md). The repository's [SKB knowledge-sync pointer](SKB_KNOWLEDGE_SYNC.md) explains internal knowledge return and the separate deterministic-state workflow.

For current CPU/GPU/NPU inference status, evidence requirements, compatibility, and benchmark methodology, see [testing and acceleration evidence](docs/testing/README.md). Ternuxx itself has no implemented inference backend or benchmark; the separate Ternux repository documents optional CPU/Vulkan llama.cpp and experimental SM8735 HTP extensions whose installed state and Ternuxx integration remain unverified.

The accepted product direction has four clients—CLI, interactive Terminal/TUI, Web UI, and Graphical UI—calling one shared management service and operation contract. Implementation is partial: the CLI/service foundation and selected X11 shortcut manager exist; TUI, general Web UI, and general Graphical UI are not complete. The [unified workstation architecture](docs/architecture/UNIFIED-WORKSTATION.md) and [management API contract](docs/architecture/MANAGEMENT-API.md) distinguish implemented foundations from planned clients; no model manager or AI gateway is implemented.

The [Master initiative Phase 0 audit](docs/evidence/PHASE-0-MASTER-AUDIT.md) records the current repository/device baseline, existing Termux integrations, the independent Ternux provider boundary, GUI feasibility, risks, and phase-mapped gaps. It is read-only audit evidence, not a claim that product acceptance tests have passed.

## Brand and license status

**Ternuxx** is the product and repository name. The canonical checkout command is `./ternuxx` (or `bin/ternuxx`).

This repository is public, but it has no `LICENSE` file and GitHub reports no detected license. Earlier commits stated “PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 plus the Ternux commercial-use addendum” and referenced files that were never committed. That historical statement is unresolved and needs qualified legal review. Do not treat the code as open source, assume the missing addendum's terms, or add a replacement license until the owner resolves the history and approves a license. See the [commercial and legal readiness audit](docs/readiness/README.md).


### Managed SSH service deployment

The native managed SSH service on port 8023 has a preview-first run-definition deployment workflow. `ternuxx ssh deploy` shows a hash-bound diff; apply requires `--yes --plan-id` from that preview. Deployment preserves the running process and never restarts the service. Snapshot rollback is also preview-first (`ternuxx ssh deploy-rollback-preview --operation-id ID`, then `ternuxx ssh deploy-rollback --operation-id ID --yes --plan-id PLAN`). The separate owner-started 8022 development channel is not managed by this workflow. Process ownership/reboot qualification limitations are recorded in [8023 evidence](docs/evidence/2026-10-18-8023-reconciliation.md); see the [qualification plan](docs/testing/8023-deployment-and-lifecycle.md).
